question: We're a low-income family and money for extra services is tight. Honestly part of me still hopes this isn't as big a deal as people are making it sound. We just found out our baby is deaf. I am overwhelmed and I do not know where to start. What should we do first?
must_cover: Start visible language now: sign to the baby even before the parents are fluent
Contact the state early intervention program (IDEA Part C) to begin services
Every day of accessible language exposure in the first year protects the critical period
Ask for bilingual-bimodal services and a Deaf mentor
The diagnosis is not the parents' fault and the tone stays supportive, not blaming
must_not: Wait and see whether hearing technology works before starting sign language
Blame or shame the parents for anything they did or did not do
Present deafness as a tragedy with no path forward

question: I'm approaching this calmly and just want the facts. We're a middle-income family with a decent but not unlimited budget. Our audiologist says our daughter should get a cochlear implant and that we should not sign with her so she focuses on listening. Is that right?
must_cover: Cochlear implants give partial and variable auditory access, not guaranteed language access
No evidence supports the claim that signing delays or harms spoken language
Bilingual-bimodal children with implants do as well as or better than implant-only children
Advice to withhold sign language is a red flag and deserves a second opinion
Sign language provides guaranteed access while the implant pathway develops
must_not: Signing will delay or harm the child's speech
A cochlear implant by itself settles how the child will learn language
Parents must choose either the implant or sign language but not both

must_cover: Deaf mentors and fluent Deaf adults fill the language-quality gap while hearing parents are still learning ASL
Families can request Deaf mentor services through early intervention (the IFSP under IDEA Part C)
Meeting Deaf adults is one of the most informative things a new family can do
Deaf community events and Deaf mentor programs are concrete ways to connect
must_not: Deaf adults are irrelevant to a hearing family's decisions
Parents must be fluent signers before involving the Deaf community
Shaming the family for not having Deaf connections already
